questions.question: The simple interest on a certain sum is 1/8 of the sum. When the number of years is equal to half the rate percentage per annum. Find the simple interest (in ₹) on ₹15000 at the same rate of simple interest for 8 years.
questions.solution:
Same R × T idea: interest one-eighth of the sum 
means R × T = 100/8 = 12.5. 
 Step 1   Use the second relation, T = R/2. 
R · (R/2) = 12.5   ⇒  R² = 25   ∴  R = 5%,  T = 2.5 yr 
 Step 2   Now the sum asked for. 
15,000 × 5 × 8 / 100 = ₹6,000

questions.question: The compound amount received on a sum of Rs 15500 at a certain annual percentage rate of simple interest in 3½ years is ₹19189. What will be the simple interest on the same amount in 6⅔years? ₹15500
questions.solution:
Step 1   Interest over the given span. 
19,189 − 15,500 = ₹3,689 over 3½ years 
 Step 2   One year's worth. 
3,689 × 2/7 = ₹1,054 
 Step 3   Multiply by the time asked. 
1,054 × 20/3 = ₹7,026.67

questions.question: A sum of ₹10,500 amounts to ₹13,825 in 3⁴/₅ years at a certain rate percent per annum simple interest. What will be the simple interest on the same sum for 5 years at double the earlier rate? ₹10,500
questions.solution:
Step 1   One year's interest. 
13,825 − 10,500 = ₹3,325 over 3⅘ yr   ⇒  3,325 × 
5/19 = ₹875 a year 
 Step 2   Double rate, five years. 
875 × 2 × 5 = ₹8,750

questions.question: A certain sum (in ₹) is invested at y% per annum for 3½ years. Had it been invested at (y + 4)% per annum at simple interest, it would have fetched ₹4,452 more as interest. What is the sum?
questions.solution:
Step 1   Write the extra interest. 
P × 4 × (7/2) / 100 = 4,452 
 Step 2   Solve for the sum. 
14P / 100 = 4,452   ∴  P = ₹31,800

questions.question: A person invested a sum of ₹10,500 at x% per annum at simple interest and a sum of ₹13,500 at (x + 2)% p.a. at simple interest. If the total interest earned on both the investments for 3 years is ₹7,650, then the rate of interest on the first investment is:
questions.solution:
Step 1   Interest on each, for 3 years. 
10,500 : 315x        13,500 : 405(x + 2) = 405x + 810 
 Step 2   Add to the given total. 
720x + 810 = 7,650   ⇒  720x = 6,840   ∴  x = 9.5%

questions.question: An amount of ₹12,000 was borrowed at simple interest, at an interest rate. After four months, ₹6000 more were added to it and the rate of interest on the total principal was doubled ₹2800 was paid as interest at the end of the year, calculate the rate of interest initially charged? ₹12,000
questions.solution:
Step 1   First four months on ₹12,000 at r%. 
12,000 × r × (4/12) / 100 = 40r 
 Step 2   Next eight months on ₹18,000 at 2r%. 
18,000 × 2r × (8/12) / 100 = 240r 
 Step 3   Total interest for the year is ₹2,800. 
280r = 2,800   ∴  r = 10%

questions.question: A sum of amounts to ₹14,395.20 at 9.25% p.a. simple interest in 5.4 years. What will be the simple interest on the same sum at 8.6% p.a. in 4.5 years?
questions.solution:
Step 1   Collapse rate and time. 
9.25 × 5.4 = 49.95%   ⇒  P × 1.4995 = 14,395.20   ∴  
P = ₹9,600 
 Step 2   Now the interest asked for. 
9,600 × 8.6 × 4.5 / 100 = ₹3,715.20

questions.question: A sum of ₹5,000 is divided into two parts such that the simple interest on the first part for 4⅕years at 6⅔% p.a. is double the simple interest on the second part for 2¾ years at 4% p.a. What is the difference between the two parts? ₹5,000
questions.solution:
Step 1   Each part's interest as a percentage of 
itself. 
first :  (21/5) yr × (20/3)% = 28% of x 
second : (11/4) yr × 4% = 11% of y 
 Step 2   The first is double the second. 
28x = 2 × 11y   ⇒  14x = 11y   ∴  x : y = 11 : 14 
 Step 3   The question asks for the DIFFERENCE of 
the parts. 
25 parts = ₹5,000 ⇒ 1 part = ₹200   ∴  (14 − 11) × 
200 = ₹600

questions.question: Suresh borrowed out a sum of money to Rakesh for 5 years at simple interest. At the end of 5 years, Rakesh paid 9/8 of the sum of Suresh to clear out the amount. Find the rate of simple interest per annum.
questions.solution:
Step 1   Interest as a fraction of P. 
I / P = 9/8 − 1 = 1/8   over 5 years 
 Step 2   Per year, then as a percentage. 
(1/8) ÷ 5 = 1/40 = 0.025   ∴  R = 2.5%

questions.question: A sum of Rs. 36,000 is divided into two parts A and B such that the simple interest at the rate of 15% p.a. on A and B after two years and four years respectively is equal. The total interest (Rs. in) received from A is: ₹36,000
questions.solution:
Step 1   Equate the two interests. 
A × 15 × 2 = B × 15 × 4   ⇒  A : B = 2 : 1 
 Step 2   Split ₹36,000 in 2 : 1. 
3 parts = 36,000 ⇒ 1 part = 12,000   ∴  A = 
₹24,000 
 Step 3   Interest received from A. 
24,000 × 15 × 2 / 100 = ₹7,200

questions.question: Sudeep invested 1/8 of a certain sum at 5% p.a. for two years and 3/5 of the sum at 6% p.a. for two years and the remaining at 10% p.a. for two years. If the total interest received is ₹1,674, then the total sum invested is?
questions.solution:
Step 1   Split 40x, computing the remainder 
rather than guessing it. 
1/8 → 5x        3/5 → 24x        rest = 40x − 5x − 24x 
= 11x 
 Step 2   Interest on each, all for 2 years. 
5x · 5% · 2 = 0.5x     24x · 6% · 2 = 2.88x     11x · 
10% · 2 = 2.2x 
 Step 3   Add to the given total. 
5.58x = 1,674   ∴  x = 300   ⇒  sum = 40x = ₹12,000

questions.question: A sum of x amounts to ₹9246 in 4 years and to ₹11,298.75 in 7½ years, at y% p.a. simple interest. The values of x and y are, respectively: x
questions.solution:
Step 1   Difference and one year's interest. 
11,298.75 − 9,246 = ₹2,052.75 over 3½ yr   ⇒  
₹586.50 a year 
 Step 2   Strip 4 years of interest off the first 
amount. 
586.50 × 4 = 2,346   ∴  x = 9,246 − 2,346 = ₹6,900 
 Step 3   Now the rate. 
y = 586.50 / 6,900 × 100 = 8.5%

questions.question: A borrowed a sum of ₹3000 from his friend B on 31 December 2007 on the condition that he would return the same after one year with simple interest at 15% per annum. However, A gets into position of returning it on 31 August 2008. How much amount had A to return to B? A
questions.solution:
Step 1   31 Dec 2007 → 31 Aug 2008. 
Jan 31 + Feb 29 + Mar 31 + Apr 30 + May 31 + Jun 
30 + Jul 31 + Aug 31 = 244 days 
 Step 2   Time = 244/366 of a year, since 2008 is a 
leap year. 
SI = 3,000 × 15 × 244 / (366 × 100) = ₹300 
 Step 3   A returns principal plus interest. 
3,000 + 300 = ₹3,300

questions.question: A sum is deposited in a bank which gives simple interest. The Sum becomes 1.25 times in 3 years. If after seven years there is a requirement of ₹760000. How much amount (in ₹) should one deposit to fulfill requirement?
questions.solution:
Step 1   Read the rate off the 3-year fact. 
3R = 25   ∴  R = 25/3 % 
 Step 2   Set the 7-year amount to the 
requirement. 
x(1 + 7 × 25/300) = 7,60,000   ⇒  19x/12 = 
7,60,000   ∴  x = ₹4,80,000

questions.question: In 't' years simple interest earned on a certain sum of money at the rate of 10% per annum is 5/8th of the principal. If the rate of interest is reduced to three fourth of 10% and the simple interest remains the same, then which of the following statements about the changed value of time is true? 't'
questions.solution:
Step 1   Find the original time. 
10t/100 = 5/8   ∴  t = 25/4 years 
 Step 2   The rate falls to three-fourths, so the 
time grows to four-thirds. 
t_new = (25/4) × (4/3) = 25/3 years

questions.question: A person invested a sum of ₹6500 at x% per annum at simple interest and a sum of ₹7500 at (x-2)% per annum at simple interest. If the total interest earned on both the investment for 3 years is ₹3,750, then the rate of interest on the first investment is:
questions.solution:
Step 1   Interest on each, for 3 years. 
65 · x · 3 + 75 · 3 · (x − 2) = 3,750 
 Step 2   Expand and solve. 
195x + 225x − 450 = 3,750   ⇒  420x = 4,200   ∴  
x = 10%
